CN01 · Continue exhibition · Editorial draft

Continuity study · House after founder

What Happens to a House After the Founder?

A house survives its founder only if the organization can distinguish what must continue, what may evolve, who may decide, which obligations remain, and what evidence authorizes each answer.

Read the exhibition

00

The proposition

House of Worth offers an unusually legible object-record sequence. The Met identifies an 1882 evening dress with Charles Frederick Worth, a 1895–1900 ball gown attributed to both Charles Frederick and Jean-Philippe Worth, and another 1898–1900 dress under the House of Worth name after Charles’s death. The records demonstrate continued house attribution and careful designer attribution; they do not prove an unbroken method, governance structure, or ownership chain.

That distinction is the center of succession. Public continuity is a claim made through names, objects, collections, stores, archives, and stories. Institutional continuity requires separate evidence for corporate authority, IP, contracts, staff knowledge, production, creditors and customers, archive custody, access, and public interpretation.

01–04

The institutional sequence

01 · STABILIZE

What cannot wait?

Secure people, payroll, orders, client commitments, facilities, insurance, accounts, credentials, physical objects, master files, and communications. Do not make permanent symbolic decisions inside the first emergency response.

PROPOSALS08S66

02 · LOCATE

Where does authority reside?

Map board and officer authority, ownership, employment, IP, licenses, estate or probate instruments, archive agreements, and operational delegations by jurisdiction and record.

PROPOSALS63S64

03 · INTERPRET

What should continue—and why?

Separate non-negotiable values, teachable method, recurring codes, historical accidents, commercial habits, and motifs. Preserve the decision logic, not a taxidermy of the last collection.

INFERENCES68S69S71

04 · ACCOUNT

Who may test the next chapter?

Define successor scope, review bodies, worker and collaborator credit, community consultation, archive citation, performance measures, correction, and removal or renewal.

PROPOSALS65

COUNTERPOINT

What this framework could get wrong

Continuation is not always the ethical or artistically honest outcome. Closing a company, preserving an archive, paying obligations, and allowing the work to become history may protect a legacy better than indefinite commercial imitation.

FIELDWORK

Do the work now

Use this as a working session, not a score.

  1. Run a 72-hour founder-absence simulation across people, money, orders, facilities, accounts, rights, archive, and public communication.
  2. Attach the governing record and backup decision-maker to every critical action.
  3. Sort house codes into values, methods, motifs, habits, and unresolved contradictions.
  4. Prepare continue, pause, license, sell, donate, and close scenarios with qualified counsel, tax, employment, conservation, and cultural advisers.

PACKAGE SYSTEM

One inquiry, six publishing forms

  • Canonical “house after founder” essay
  • Fifteen-minute Worth-to-governance film
  • Twelve-frame 72-hour succession carousel
  • Five founder-absence shorts
  • House Continuity Stress Test

Finished platform treatments

01

LONG VIDEO — Put four Worth records on a timeline. State only what the records prove, then reveal the missing governance layer. Run the house through stabilize, locate, interpret, account.

02

SHORT 01 — “A name continuing is evidence of continuity. It is not proof that everything continued.” Split attribution, company, method, people, archive, rights, and obligations.

03

SHORT 02 — “The first succession decision may be to pause.” Stabilize obligations before announcing a creative heir.

04

CAROUSEL — THE FOUNDER IS ABSENT / PEOPLE / ORDERS / MONEY / KEYS / IP / ARCHIVE / AUTHORITY / METHOD / SUCCESSOR / CORRECTION / CONTINUE OR CLOSE.

05

NEWSLETTER — Subject: What exactly survives when the founder does not? Use the Worth record sequence to distinguish public continuity from institutional continuity.

06

BOARD / ESTATE BRIEF — Six scenarios—continue, pause, license, sell, donate, close—with responsible authority, affected stakeholders, evidence, risks, and counsel gates.

Reading protocol

Every material statement carries an evidence label and point-of-claim source links. Interpretation is never presented as source fact. Legal sections identify their jurisdiction; state, foreign, contractual, beneficial-ownership, validity, priority, and disputed-fact questions remain counsel-review gates. This exhibition is educational and does not provide legal, conservation, or business advice.
